approach: Add a family check to Config::validate (crates/athena-data/src/config.rs:639), which Config::parse calls on every load (config.rs:616-619). It looks at the model names in the roles (reader, producer_default, producer_allowed, verifier and hard_producer_model). It matches case-insensitively on the substrings opus, sonnet and haiku. If a family is absent it returns a new variant ConfigError::ModelFamily(&'static str), placed after the HardProducerNotAllowed check (config.rs:670-674). The [models.names] display table is not a role and is not read, so a stale display name cannot hide a missing role. config.rs unit tests build the failing configs from REPO_CONFIG text (config.rs:888) with one family removed and assert Config::parse returns ModelFamily("haiku"), ("sonnet") or ("opus"). The unmodified text must still parse. A new integration test crates/athena-core/tests/model_roster.rs reads the repository athena.toml through athena_data::Config::parse and asserts that the roles cover all three families. The same file asserts jev::ENDPOINT contains ai-gateway.vercel.sh and jev::MODEL == "typesafe-ai/jev" (jev.rs:31-33; jev.rs is unchanged). The spec entry OLY-B-SET-02 (docs/spec.toml:2020-2025) gets a real mechanism and a measure ending `status: not shown`. A line `athena-core --test model_roster 5.00` goes into xtask/shard-timings.txt, because checked_in_timings_cover_every_workspace_test_unit asserts the file's units equal the workspace targets exactly (xtask/tests/ci_shards.rs:410-421). A CHANGELOG entry is added under [Unreleased] / Added. athena.toml, defaults.toml, workflows, jev.rs and lib.rs are not touched. briefs.rs: the only model names there are plain struct fixtures (briefs.rs:1477-1478, 3549-3550) that never go through Config::parse, so no edit is needed; the producer leaves it unchanged unless a test shows otherwise.

decisions.choice: Enforce the roles in Config::validate with a new ConfigError::ModelFamily(&'static str) variant, matching by lowercase substring on reader, producer_default, producer_allowed, verifier and hard_producer_model.
decisions.reason: validate is the non-test reader every load reaches: Config::parse (config.rs:616), config_at in the gate (athena-gate/src/lib.rs:184), JobConfig::at (capability.rs:41) and admission (admission.rs:933). A real athena.toml that loses a family is therefore refused wherever it is loaded, and nothing new has to be read by anything else. The check needs no list of model ids, so a model upgrade such as claude-opus-5-6 keeps passing.

rejected.option: A hard-coded ROSTER constant in jev.rs, checked only by a test (the rejected prior job 20261030-001211-6mzd)
rejected.why: Nothing read it, so removing a model from the real config left the test green.

rejected.option: Match exact ids such as claude-opus-5-5
rejected.why: Every model upgrade would need a code change, and the spec says Opus, Sonnet and Haiku, not a version.

rejected.option: Also count the keys of [models.names] as roles
rejected.why: That table is only display text for trailers (athena.toml:28-32). A stale entry there would hide a missing role.

decisions.choice: Keep Jev shadow-only. The Jev clause of the requirement is shown only by asserting the existing constants jev::ENDPOINT and jev::MODEL in model_roster.rs.
decisions.reason: The brief puts making Jev decide real work out of scope, and jev.rs is unchanged. Reading the constants from the real module reuses them instead of copying them.

rejected.option: Add Jev to [models] or to the family check
rejected.why: It would change athena.toml and make Jev a model that does real work, which is out of scope.

rejected.why: The brief requires `cargo test -p athena-core --test model_roster`, which needs an integration test file.

risks.risk: A model name that does not carry opus, sonnet or haiku (for example a future alias) would be refused as missing a family.
risks.mitigation: The error names the family and the rule. The match is case-insensitive substring, so version bumps (claude-opus-5-6) and vendor prefixes pass. A real alias change would need a deliberate edit of the rule.

risks.risk: JobConfig::at or config_at parsing an athena.toml from an old commit that lacks a family would now fail.
risks.mitigation: The current athena.toml has all three families, and the repository's verifier has been an Opus model in the config the tests load. The producer should run the full `cargo test --locked` (tests that load config at fixture commits start from the real athena.toml). HISTORY.txt cannot show old file contents.

risks.risk: A text-replacement test passes for the wrong reason if the replace pattern does not match, leaving the config unchanged, or if another error fires first.
risks.mitigation: The helper asserts the replaced text differs from the original and each case asserts the exact ModelFamily variant, so VerifierCanProduce or DefaultProducerNotAllowed cannot satisfy it. The opus case uses a verifier outside producer_allowed.

risks.risk: The briefs.rs deliverable has no needed edit, so the producer may be tempted to touch it for nothing.
risks.mitigation: The plan states it stays unchanged; any edit must be tied to a failing test.

risks.risk: ci.yml shard balancing: a new target with an estimated 5.00 s is a guess.
risks.mitigation: The file header already marks values as estimates; the line is labelled the same way.

demonstrations.method: New unit tests in the config.rs tests module (which imports super::*, config.rs:885). A helper takes REPO_CONFIG, applies line replacements to the [models] lines with replacen, and asserts each replacement changed the text so a misfire cannot pass silently. Cases: (haiku) producer_allowed becomes ["claude-sonnet-5-5"]; (sonnet) reader, producer_default and hard_producer_model become claude-haiku-5-5 and producer_allowed becomes ["claude-haiku-5-5"]; (opus) verifier becomes claude-other-5-5, which is outside producer_allowed so VerifierCanProduce does not fire first. The [models.names] table still lists all three, which shows the check ignores it. Each case asserts matches!(Config::parse(&text), Err(ConfigError::ModelFamily("haiku"/"sonnet"/"opus"))) and the error string names the family. A control test asserts REPO_CONFIG unchanged parses. A second control uses uppercase names (e.g. Claude-Haiku) to show case-insensitivity.
demonstrations.observes: The three removal cases return the matching ModelFamily error; the control parses.
demonstrations.fails_without: If the ModelFamily check in Config::validate is deleted, all three removal cases parse successfully and the matches! assertions fail. Without the assertion that each replacen changed the text, a test could pass for the wrong reason, so the helper asserts the text differs.
demonstrations.seam: Entry point: Config::parse (config.rs:616), which calls validate. Fixture: REPO_CONFIG = include_str!(athena.toml) (config.rs:888), modified as text, with no fake. The seam exists today. The new helper is added in plan step 3.

demonstrations.method: New integration test crates/athena-core/tests/model_roster.rs. It reads athena.toml from Path::new(env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR")).join("../..") (the same approach as crates/athena-data/tests/repo_config.rs:10-15) and calls athena_data::Config::parse, so it goes through the real loader and validate. It then asserts the lowercased names across reader, producer_default, producer_allowed and verifier contain opus, sonnet and haiku separately. It also asserts a copy of the text with the haiku entry removed from producer_allowed is refused with athena_data::config::ConfigError::ModelFamily (a mutation check on the real loader in the same file). Finally it asserts athena_core::jev::ENDPOINT contains "ai-gateway.vercel.sh" and athena_core::jev::MODEL == "typesafe-ai/jev".
demonstrations.observes: All assertions pass on the repository files.
demonstrations.fails_without: If a family is removed from the real athena.toml or the check in validate is removed, the parse or the mutation assertion fails. If jev::ENDPOINT or jev::MODEL changes, the Jev asserts fail.
